_comment: Input to `besu operator generate-blockchain-config` — produces the 8470 genesis
plus one keypair per validator. See docs/multinode-tiny-chain-design.md.
chainId 8470: a NEW id, deliberately not the live 8469 (which production settles
on and which is a single anvil process). Running both is the whole migration plan.
P1 is HEADER mode: the validator set lives in the genesis extraData. Contract mode
(validatorcontractaddress + getValidators(), which is what makes validator entry
permissionless) is P2 — Besu supports transitioning between the two at a future
block, so shipping header-mode first costs no rework.
blockperiodseconds 2 matches the live chain, so payment-path latency assumptions
(x402 settles BEFORE serving) carry over unchanged.
zeroBaseFee: gas is FREE but still METERED — gasLimit is real. Free-and-unmetered
would be an unbounded write channel once anyone can validate (design doc 0.1).
4 validators is the minimum meaningful QBFT set: f = floor((n-1)/3) = 1, so it
tolerates exactly one Byzantine node. A 3-node set has f=0 and tolerates nothing.

config._shanghaiTime_comment: REQUIRED, and the trap is silent: besu's own dev genesis stops at londonBlock, but solc 0.8.24 emits PUSH0 (0x5f), a Shanghai opcode. On a London chain EVERY contract deploy dies with 'Invalid opcode: 0x5f' — the chain itself looks perfectly healthy, so the failure reads as a broken deploy script. Post-merge forks are TIMESTAMP-keyed, not block-keyed, and genesis timestamp is 0, so 0 activates it from block 1. Matching the live 8469 (anvil, modern fork) also means a contract that works in prod can't fail here for a reason prod never had.

genesis._gasLimit_comment: 30,000,000 — mainnet-scale on purpose. Free gas still needs a REAL ceiling, or 'metered' is a word with no number behind it (design §0.1). Was 0x1fffffffffffff, which metered nothing.
genesis._mixHash_comment: The QBFT/IBFT magic value — ASCII 'ctical byzantine fault tolerance', EXACTLY 32 bytes. Besu rejects any other value outright; a 33rd byte fails with 'Invalid mixHash'.
_alloc_comment: NOT decoration, and NOT (only) about paying for gas. Proven by controlled test on this
devnet: a sender whose account does not exist in state has its txs accepted by the pool,
gossiped to every peer, and then NEVER selected into a block — silently, forever. The pool
reports them pending, blocks keep being produced empty, and no error is logged anywhere.
Funding the SAME sender with 1 wei makes the SAME zero-fee tx mine immediately.
So zero-price gas does not mean zero-balance senders. Anyone who wants to submit a tx here
— including a joiner staking from its validator key — needs a nonzero balance first. That's
a real onboarding step (P5 must ship a drip), not a footnote.
